headline: California Achieves Historic Drop in Unsheltered Homelessness
meta_description: California recorded its largest reduction in unsheltered homelessness in 16 years, with 8,391 fewer people on the streets in 2025.
summary_short: California's unsheltered homelessness fell by 8,391 people in 2025—the largest decline in 16 years. Over 110,000 have found permanent housing since 2023.
body:
California recorded its largest reduction in unsheltered homelessness in 16 years in 2025, with 8,391 fewer people living on the streets.

The progress reflects sustained effort across the state. More than 110,000 people have moved into permanent housing since 2023, representing a shift in how communities address homelessness through housing-first approaches.

While the snippet doesn't reveal specific programs or regions driving the change, the scale of movement—from streets into stable homes—points to coordinated action at scale. A 16-year milestone suggests this isn't a temporary fluctuation but a meaningful reversal of a long-standing trend.
quick_facts: 8,391 fewer unsheltered people in California in 2025
Largest reduction in unsheltered homelessness in 16 years
110,000+ people moved into permanent housing since 2023
